spore game sourced

Spore

A five-stage game in which the player guides a species from cell to galactic empire, building its body, vehicles, and buildings in part-based editors whose creations are shared automatically through the Sporepedia.

2008MaxisEcosystem / evolutioncluster c118 mechanics
this record asyaml sourcemarkdownjson

core loop

eat to earn DNA points -> edit body parts to change abilities -> befriend or fight other species -> stage completes and grants consequence traits -> next stage changes the rules -> colonize and terraform planets -> creations upload to the Sporepedia and populate other players' galaxies

design notes

Spore's evolution is player design rather than selection: body parts bought with DNA points set speed, attack, and social abilities directly, and nothing is inherited by differential survival. Its distinctive system is the part-based editors (18 share one interface) whose creations are stored as compact descriptions of a few kilobytes and reconstructed procedurally, which let Maxis upload every creation and redistribute them as the inhabitants of other players' galaxies (over 100 million by May 2009). Each of the five stages swaps in a different genre's rules, and play style in each stage assigns consequence traits that carry forward.

relations

8 stored edges
uses

Content sharing

Every creation uploads automatically to the Sporepedia and is redistributed to populate other players' worlds, so other players' designs fill the galaxy without manual import.

core
uses

Milestone unlocks

Each stage ends at a progress threshold and hands the species to a new rule set (cell, creature, tribal, civilization, space), with three consequence traits awarded from how aggressive or social the player was.

core
uses

Modular assembly

Creature, building, and vehicle editors assemble parts such as mouths, legs, and arms whose choice sets abilities, diet options, and stats; textures and animation are applied procedurally to the assembled topology.

core
uses

Direct avatar control

The player directly steers the cell, the creature, and later a spaceship.

supporting
uses

Faction diplomacy

Creature-stage species, tribes, nations, and space empires such as the Grox can be befriended through social actions or conquered.

supporting
uses

Procedural terrain

supporting
uses

Terraforming

In the space stage rocky planets can be terraformed, their ecosystems changed, and features such as mountains and lakes added.

supporting
uses

Unit commands

Tribal and civilization stages switch to commanding up to 12 tribe members, then vehicles and cities.
